name: Battle of Actium

phases.title: Antony's fleet comes out and forms line
phases.text: Octavian's fleet waited beyond the straits. Antony led his ships out through the straits and they formed a line, with Cleopatra's squadron behind them, and stayed quiet.

phases.title: Octavian steers to the right
phases.text: After a short hesitation Octavian ordered his ships to steer to the right and pass the enemy's ships. Fearing that his line would be surrounded, Antony was forced to give the order to attack.

phases.title: Sosius attacks and Octavian's left stays out of range
phases.text: Sosius opened the attack from Antony's left wing. Antony hoped to drive back Agrippa's wing at the north end of his line with his biggest ships, but Octavian's fleet stayed out of range.

phases.title: The fleets fight through the afternoon
phases.text: The two lines closed after midday and fought on all afternoon. Antony's larger ships rained missiles on the smaller ones, which closed in, shot at the crews and drew off again, and neither side gained a clear result.

phases.title: Cleopatra's squadron sails for the open sea
phases.text: Cleopatra's squadron, in the rear, took no part in the fighting and retreated to the open sea. A breeze sprang up in the right direction and the ships were soon out of sight.

phases.title: Antony follows and the rest are taken
phases.text: Antony thought all was lost and followed the fleeing squadron. He moved to a smaller vessel and slipped away with a few ships as escort, and the ships left behind were captured or sunk.

note: Antony's fleet came out of the straits and Octavian's waited beyond them, so Antony is drawn to the east and Octavian to the west, with north at the top; the accounts give the wings and the north end of Antony's line but no compass bearings. The land is drawn only as the accounts name it and is placed by judgement. The accounts give two sets of ship numbers, and J. M. Carter gives a second account, in which Antony formed a horseshoe near the shore and broke out through a gap in Octavian's line while his own ships spread north and south. Cleopatra's route to the open sea and Antony's route through the line are not described, so both are drawn as straight lines. Octavian's order to steer to the right is drawn as a small shift of his right wing.
